content:
BHU uncovers A 70 years old archaeological treasure from Rajghat.

Archaeological Artifacts- Include sculptures, ancient coins, tools, stamp seals, and objects made of copper, ivory, and bone, as well as pottery believed to be nearly 3,000 years old. 

Inscriptions and Scripts - Several seals bear inscriptions, including in Brahmi script, offering potential insights into ancient governance, trade and economic systems.

Around 3,000 glass slides and over 5,000 
photographic negatives documenting archaeological sites such as Rajghat, Ajanta, Ellora, Ratnagiri and Manjhi.

Why rajghat is important? 

Ancient Varanasi - Rajghat, near the Ganga–Varuna confluence, was an important settlement of ancient Varanasi, associated with the Kashi Mahajanapada. 

Long Cultural History - Excavations indicate six cultural periods, from around 800 BCE to the medieval period. 

Recent Discovery - A human skeleton recovered from Rajghat and preserved in a 
sealed box for nearly 70 years was recently opened for study.

Samples were collected for genetic and bioarchaeological analysis to understand the people who lived in Varanasi around 1,000 years ago.

Archaeological Survey of India, History Education at the Council of Europe,
LinkedIn News, Banaras Hindu University (BHU), Varanasi
comment: Beyond the artifacts, the real value lies in preserving context—cataloguing provenance, excavation records and scientific data will determine how much future research can learn from these findings.
